definitions.meaning: removed or extracted, as something drawn out of a larger whole
daydreaming, lost in thought and inattentive

explanation.surface: Something gets removed while its owner is daydreaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dictionary senses: extracted, and absent-minded or preoccupied.

clue.text: This can provide an image that includes love — for oneself?

definitions.text: This can provide an image that includes love — for oneself?

indicators.note: the phrase takes the zero letter into itself before shuffling
the letters of the phrase can be rearranged to provide something else, signalling a reshuffle

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A riddle about a picture that contains affection directed at oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: AN IMAGE with O placed inside is rearranged under 'can provide'; the whole clue also describes the answer, an image of love for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsessive self-regard is literally a mania for the ego, an excessive love for oneself.

clue.text: Left one extremely out of sorts

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
very and extremely are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone who was left behind feels thoroughly unwell and grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverish, irritable or queasy, as if the liver were troubling one; an informal British adjective.

definitions.meaning: to pick out or notice something
an exact place, as in 'the very place'

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means detect or notice; as a noun it means a particular place.

clue.text: A strict, or a liberal, gentleman?

indicators.note: liberal suggests a free, loose treatment of the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether a gentleman is a disciplinarian or a progressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' reads as a political label opposite 'strict', but it is the anagram signal; the question mark flags that gentleman is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman in the old sense was a man of noble birth, so a nobleman fits as an example.

clue.text: It currently controls rose that is rambling

indicators.note: a rambling rose sprawls in all directions, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A climbing rose that sprawls everywhere is in charge right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currently' seems to mean 'at present' but means 'regarding electric current'; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A variable resistor is a device for regulating the electric current in a circuit.

parts.note: cheeky here means found on the cheek, not impudent: a charming little hollow on a face

explanation.surface: Praises an impudent yet appealing trait in someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A small natural hollow in the cheek, often thought charming, is a facial feature on the cheek.

clue.text: Boss to pore over books endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the verb is dropped

parts.note: to study is to read books closely

explanation.surface: A manager tells someone to keep their nose in their books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager but is the ornamental knob sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised ornamental knob or button, as is a decorative metal stud.

clue.text: American stars encountered in amusement park

definitions.meaning: the American name for the seven bright stars of the Plough constellation
a switchback roller coaster at a fairground

explanation.surface: Celebrities from the US are spotted at a theme park.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the US star group called the Plough in Britain and a fairground roller-coaster ride.

indicators.note: one letter is placed among the others, inside the word for many

parts.note: a host is a great number, a multitude
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Raise one person above the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or lift something up, often with ropes or tackle, is a synonym of elevate.
It means a violent storm and is also the title of the play Shakespeare wrote about a shipwreck.

clue.text: Skinhead frisked and betrayed to the police

parts.note: read as the head of skin, its first letter S
to frisk is to skip and leap playfully, so frisked means hopped

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed thug is searched and then informed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frisked' suggests a police search, but here means leaped about; 'Skinhead' is split into skin's head.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: to shop someone is to inform on them to the authorities.

clue.text: Trouble caused by a small number in New York

indicators.note: the abbreviation for number sits in the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: NO is the short form of number, small meaning abbreviated

explanation.surface: Bother arises from a modest figure in a big American city.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to irritate or bother them, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Winning measure from brusque school principal

parts.note: short with someone means curt or brusque
the head teacher runs a school

explanation.surface: A curt head teacher hands out a prize-winning measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing, a tiny winning margin less than the length of a horse's head.

clue.text: Christian virtue fills a need, somehow

indicators.note: in some way or other, so the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A Christian virtue somehow meets a need.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from one's own desires is a classic ascetic virtue in Christian teaching.

parts.note: an opening is the opposite of a shutting, so the word reads as not-closing, as well as a revealing of facts

explanation.surface: A startling discovery right at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A revealing of hidden facts is a revelation, and the word splits as dis- plus closure, an un-closing.

definitions.meaning: commercial salesmen were called travellers, so their stories belong to them

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means far-fetched stories, and travelling salesmen, once called commercial travellers, tell such stories.

parts.note: a deerstalker is a hunting cap with flaps that come down over the sides of the head; comedowns usually means disappointments

explanation.surface: Hunters of deer suffer humiliating setbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: The side flaps of a deerstalker cap fold down over the wearer's ears.

clue.text: Bear I let out — yes, let out!

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frees a bear and insists on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'out' signals the anagram; the second 'let out', after 'yes', is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To free or release someone is to let them out.

definitions.meaning: to cast doubt on, refuse to believe

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means disgrace; as a verb it means to disbelieve or show something to be false.

indicators.note: the letters of the word are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A spring of water alters its route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' could be a season or a leap, but here it is where water rises.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is the origin of a stream, its fountainhead.

parts.note: a babe is a baby

explanation.surface: A baby has been abandoned in a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the city where the tower reaching to heaven was built was named for confusion of tongues.

parts.note: big and great are synonyms
Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A fine young woman is getting married illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying while already married is the crime of having two spouses at once.

parts.note: Maud is a girl's name

indicators.note: the word for nothing is taken back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A girl retracts her offer of nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearfully or weakly emotional, especially when drunk: a synonym for mawkish sentimentality.

clue.text: Doctor about to get an increase

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A doctor is about to receive a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' gives RE and 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional amount, as in asking for some extra; the noun sense of an increased quantity.

definitions.meaning: best wishes sent at the close of a letter

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means looks at or considers; as a plural noun it is a friendly greeting, as in 'kind ___'.

clue.text: Storm caused by parking on drive

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: to ram is to drive or force something in
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A car park causes a storm by being built on a driveway.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramp is to rage or rampage, to storm about angrily.

parts.note: re means concerning or about
capital means of the head and investment means clothing, so a hat is head-wear

explanation.surface: A brief report on a financial investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital investment' sounds financial, but means something put on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A recapitulation, abbreviated, is a brief restatement of the main points.

clue.text: Graduate repeatedly brought in to reform old university

indicators.note: the doubled degree is brought into the middle of the word for reform

parts.note: to reform something is to alter it

indicators.note: the degree is written twice in succession

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate degree

explanation.surface: A graduate returns again and again to reform their old college.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'nourishing mother', the term for the school or university one attended.
